newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES QUOTED LARGELY STABLE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES QUOTED LARGELY STABLE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market held largely steady on Thursday despite a further drop in the level of liquidity in the system, dealers said.
"The market still looks a bit tight at the moment. Yesterday we closed only with a small amount in surplus. But rates are still stable at their previous levels," said one dealer.
He said discount houses were selling treasury bills unchanged at 17.85 percent and bankers acceptances were also being bought and sold at a steady 18.75 and 18.50 percent respectively.

Negotiable certificates of deposit maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days edged up to 19.25 percent (buying) from 19 percent but their selling rate remained at Wednesday's 18.75 percent. Call money, at 18.50 percent, was also unchanged.
Figures from the central Reserve Bank showed a fall in the pre-settlement surplus to Z$11.3 million from Z$33 million.
